The aligned view (fnasm 0x1f0:0x230 --diff) confirms the rows are genuinely paired, so this one is real, not a pairing artifact. IT IS NOT A WRONG FIELD. The cause is visible at +0x0198, where the target emits `lwzu r0,96(r24)` - a load-with-update that advances r24 by 96 as a side effect, so from that point the target addresses the element at 0(r24) while our non-updating form still addresses it at 96(r24). Both compute the same effective address; the difference is the load-update idiom, i.e. the recorded lwzu-idiom class, and the source lever is a `p += 96` compound assignment feeding the load rather than an indexed read. NOT A SHORT PATH: this is one cluster of 55 structural rows plus 3 unpaired, so closing it will not approach exact on its own.
